name: Pat Fraser
life: “I still remember my old business partner closing the shutter early for me.” On Wednesday, near Juniper Street, Pat knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I heard their conversation through the wall and realized I owed my old shop partner a call.
appearance: Pat is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and a small notch in the left eyebrow. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with one cuff folded back twice, Pat presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Pat admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Pat learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To call the former shop partner.
family: Anton Shah is Pat’s cousin. Pat is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Anton calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The waiting-room plant*, Anton says, “I used the leaves to teach shadows to a child in isolation.”
connections: Eli Aranda. A conversation heard through the wall finds its way back into a school costume story.
